name: Unsane
label: AmRep
lede: A Lower East Side trio that put a decapitated subway corpse on its first cover, then got a skateboard-wipeout video that cost a couple hundred dollars onto MTV.

eras.title: Scum rock from Alphabet City
eras.text: Chris Spencer, Pete Shore and Charlie Ondras start out at Sarah Lawrence College and end up in the heroin-and-hardcore East Village of the late 80s. Their first album vanishes with a label owner; their second puts a subway corpse on the sleeve.

years.h: Three Sarah Lawrence students start Lawn-Chair-Blisters
years.p: [[Chris Spencer|9a653ece-8339-4e2e-b893-106b13c4dbc3]], Pete Shore and [[Charlie Ondras|0405bd1e-7edd-41b9-bc0b-ca8ef8f464ba]] form a trio at Sarah Lawrence College and soon rename it Unsane.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band to 1988 and the first name to Lawn-Chair-Blisters. Spencer plays guitar and sings, Shore plays bass, Ondras drums.

The trio moves into the East Village, where Spencer has said in interviews that he shared an apartment with Ondras on 8th and D, a building where heroin was sold openly in the lobby.

years.h: Debut album Improvised Munitions goes missing with its label boss
years.p: Unsane record their first album with Wharton Tiers for Circuit Records, and the label owner disappears after handing Spencer a test pressing at the Pyramid Club.
years.xp:
Spencer told Louder and Bandcamp Daily that the Long Island label's owner, Ernie, vanished, which he links to a cocaine habit and debts. The album stayed unreleased for over 30 years.

A test pressing turned up later, and Unsane's own Lamb Unlimited label issued it in 2021 as Improvised Munitions & Demo.

years.big: Scum rock, not a career plan.
years.h: East Village neighbors: Cop Shoot Cop, Surgery, Helmet
years.p: Unsane come up in a scene of CBGB, ABC No Rio and the Pyramid Club, alongside Cop Shoot Cop, Surgery and Helmet.
years.xp: Spencer told Louder that New York in the 80s was lawless, and that he was close friends with Sean McDonell of Surgery. Ondras also played on two [[Boss Hog|57648c1f-335d-4216-ba82-508b23b3bcf4]] records, Drinkin', Lechin' & Lyin' (1989) and Cold Hands (1990).

years.h: Gerard Cosloy sees a CBGB set and signs them to Matador
years.p: A CBGB show gets the band a deal with Matador Records through label co-founder Gerard Cosloy.

years.h: A decapitated body on the subway tracks
years.p: Unsane lands on Matador with a cover photo of a decapitated corpse on subway tracks, recorded in January at Fun City Studios.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the cover image came from someone who worked on the actual criminal investigation. AllMusic's Patrick Kennedy called the record a brilliant and daring debut that mixed the harshness of [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]] and [[Foetus|934c6bbc-3fc4-4d4a-9280-f02856da0e12]] with punk and classic-rock hooks.

Spencer told Vice that using real blood in art was taboo in the AIDS era; the trio saw itself as making exploitation-movie noise.

eras.title: Charlie's last summer, and a Matador-Atlantic album
eras.text: Ondras dies in June 1992, Vinnie Signorelli takes over from him behind the kit, and the band cuts Total Destruction for Matador and Atlantic. Pete Shore leaves in 1994.

years.h: Singles 89-92 collects the early 7-inches
years.p: Matador issues Singles 89–92, thirteen tracks including "Burn", "Urge to Kill" and "Blood Boy".

years.h: Charlie Ondras dies at the New Music Seminar
years.p: Ondras, 25, died of a heroin overdose while attending the 1992 New Music Seminar in New York, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Louder reported that Spencer described Ondras as an occasional user, while Spencer himself was more heavily addicted at the time. The band had been on tour supporting the debut record.

years.h: Vinnie Signorelli arrives from Foetus and Swans
years.p: Drummer [[Vinnie Signorelli|8e1d0d17-1272-4418-ace5-3d6f3bde0daf]], who played with [[Foetus|934c6bbc-3fc4-4d4a-9280-f02856da0e12]] and [[Swans|3285dc48-9505-469d-ad8a-bdf2d3dba632]], replaces Ondras after Anthony DeLuca sits in briefly.

years.h: Total Destruction, recorded for $25,000
years.p: Total Destruction comes out on Matador and Atlantic, tracked at BC Studio in Brooklyn with Martin Bisi.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the band kept the budget low to limit what it would owe Atlantic. The video for "Body Bomb", with explosives imagery, was banned from MTV; Vox later put the cover on its list of the fifty worst sleeves.

years.h: Pete Shore leaves; Dave Curran takes the bass
years.p: [[Dave Curran|7ce793e3-5530-4e32-a3f8-1b6661fe3205]] replaces original bassist Pete Shore, who left in 1994 for reasons Wikipedia does not give.

eras.title: AmRep, Scrape and the Vienna trip
eras.text: Unsane hole up in Minneapolis to make Scattered, Smothered & Covered for AmRep, get an unlikely MTV hit, move to Relapse, and end the decade with Spencer in surgery.

years.h: Scattered, Smothered & Covered, made in the AmRep basement
years.p: Unsane record for Amphetamine Reptile Records in Minneapolis from January to May, with engineer Tim Mac.
years.xp: Label boss [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]] ran a studio in the AmRep offices. Spencer told Vice the band holed up there for weeks between tours during a Minneapolis winter. Decibel put the record in its Hall of Fame in 2012; the title nods to a Waffle House order.

years.h: Scrape: skateboard wipeouts, a couple hundred dollars, MTV rotation
years.p: The video for "Scrape" splices rehearsal footage with skaters bailing, and gets heavy MTV play.
years.xp: Wikipedia's band page puts the cost at $200; the album page says $169. The clip was one of two videos for the album, the other for "Alleged".

years.h: Dave Curran and Vinnie Signorelli become the rhythm section
years.p: With Curran on bass and Signorelli on drums, the trio stays fixed for the next twenty-plus years, minus one hiatus.

years.h: Occupational Hazard, on Relapse, mixed by Dave Sardy
years.p: Relapse Records releases the fourth album, recorded at Excello Studios in Brooklyn with Billy Anderson and Bruce Hathaway.
years.xp: Spencer has said the record was partly cut analog and remixed at a midtown studio by Dave Sardy. AllMusic's Blake Butler compared the record to getting hit by a semi.

q: They thought I was military because I was wearing camo pants.
years.h: Spencer is attacked outside a Vienna bar
years.p: Spencer was attacked by four people after a Vienna show and needed major surgery for internal bleeding, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Spencer told PopMatters that his attackers thought his camouflage pants meant he was military, and that surgeons had to lift out his organs.

He wore a supportive girdle on the 10-month tour that followed. Wikipedia says the injury and heavy touring led the band to take a long break.

eras.title: Cutthroats, tattoos and a long break
eras.text: The band goes quiet. Spencer moves to California, Signorelli opens a tattoo shop in Queens, and Curran keeps playing.

years.h: Side projects: Cutthroats 9, J.J. Paradise Players Club, a tattoo shop
years.p: Spencer and Curran make an album as The Cutthroats 9 for Man's Ruin, and Signorelli opens a tattoo shop in Middle Village, Queens.

eras.title: Back and louder
eras.text: Unsane regroup in 2003 and make five more albums for Relapse, Ipecac, Alternative Tentacles and Southern Lord.

years.h: Blood Run on Relapse
years.p: Blood Run is the first Unsane studio album since the break.

years.h: Visqueen on Ipecac, produced with Andrew Schneider
years.p: The sixth album comes out on Ipecac Recordings; Pitchfork's Marc Masters called the sound intact but slicker.

years.h: Wreck on Alternative Tentacles, tracked in Brooklyn
years.p: Wreck is recorded at Translator Audio with Andrew Schneider, and the band tours with the Melvins in April and May.

years.h: Spencer forms UXO with Today Is the Day's Steve Austin
years.p: Between Unsane albums, Spencer starts UXO with Steve Austin of [[Today Is the Day|c5790c27-5808-42a2-b409-5395b56c209f]]; a self-titled album follows in 2016 on Reptilian Records.

years.h: Sterilize, written in three cities
years.p: Southern Lord releases Sterilize, made with songs traded as audio files between band members living apart.
years.xp: Curran told Vice the band wrote separately and sent parts back and forth, from more than 90 minutes of material.

years.h: Spencer leaves Unsane and starts Human Impact
years.p: Spencer announces he is leaving the band and forming Human Impact with Phil Puleo, Chris Pravdica and Jim Coleman.

eras.title: The band starts again from the beginning
eras.text: Spencer revives Unsane in 2021 with a new rhythm section and a new label to reissue the old catalog in order.

years.h: Unsane return with Eric Cooper and Jon Syverson
years.p: Spencer reforms Unsane with bassist Eric Cooper and drummer Jon Syverson, focusing on early material.

years.h: Lamb Unlimited puts out Improvised Munitions & Demo
years.p: The band's own label debuts with the lost 1989 record, a project of reissuing the catalog chronologically.
years.xp: Spencer runs the label with longtime manager Todd Cote. He told Bandcamp Daily the plan is to go chronologically, one release at a time.
